items.title: Public Meeting to Consider an Official Plan Amendment & Zoning
notes: Amendment

items.title: OP01/25 and RZ01/25
notes: Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of this public meeting is to present and receive public input regarding proposed official plan amendment and zoning by-law amendment broadly affecting lands in the Township.
He noted the purpose of the proposed official plan amendment is to change Section C.5- Housing Policies to include a new section C.5.8- Additional Residential Units.
The effect of the official plan amendment is to include policies regarding Additional Residential Units (ARUs) on land where residential uses are permitted.

Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to allow Additional Residential Units (ARUs), both attached and detached, on lands where residential uses are permitted and provide associated regulations. And further to permit “M1-Service Industrial” uses to be added to the list of permitted uses in “M2 – General Industrial”.
The effect of the amendment is to implement zoning regulations necessary to facilitate Additional Residential Units and to add permitted uses in the M2 - Industrial zone.

Mayor Watters indicated if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of the County of Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the official plan amendment is adopted, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision.

He indicated if a person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the proposed official plan amendment is adopted, the person or public body may not be added as a party to the hearing of an appeal before the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to add the person or pubic body as a party.

He indicated if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision.

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submission at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as the party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters advised if anyone wishes to be notified of the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington in respect of the proposed zoning by- law amendment, a written request must be filed with the Municipal Clerk of the Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, Ontario, N0B 1S0.

He advised if the official plan amendment is adopted, it will be forwarded to the County of Wellington for approval. If you wish to be notified of the decision of The Corporation of the County of Wellington in respect of the proposed official plan amendment, you must make a written request to the Director, Planning and Development Department, County of Wellington, 74 Woolwich Street, Guelph, Ontario, N1H 3T9.

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before March 20, 2025. She indicated a copy was also placed in the Wellington Advertiser on March 20, 2025.
She further confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on March 20, 2025.

Mayor Watters called on Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development to present the application. He outlined the legislative requirements and changes to current regulations regarding additional residential units (ARUs). He illustrated the various ARU configurations permitted.

B. Salmon also outlined the M2 zoning permitted use changes, indicating any M1 industrial zone permitted uses than are not already permitted by the M2 zone will be added to the M2 zone list of permitted uses.

Mayor Watters indicated there are no delegations registered and asked if there is anyone present wishing to speak to the application. There being none, Mayor Watters asked if Members of Council had any questions.

Staff responded to questions related to short term rentals associated with additional rental units, wording changes from accessory apartments to additional residential units, and the difference between garden suites and additional residential units.
Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and advised Council will be considering the by-law later this evening.
Mayor Watters declared the meeting adjourned.

items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters noted up coming changes to the recycling program for residential areas as well as the industrial, commercial and institutional areas.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Members of Council provided updates regarding the ongoing activities of the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee, the Elora BIA, and the Economic Prosperity & Growth Committee.

items.title: Melinda Croft, resident and business owner expressed concerns with
notes: the draft short-term rental by-law. She indicated she supports licensing and regulating short-term rentals (STRs) but is not supportive of the draft by-law under consideration. M. Croft feels the draft by-law is an extreme transition from the current status and is not in favour of over regulation. She is supportive of the revenue generated from licensing to be applied towards parking, garbage, etc., and not staff resources. She feels the regulations/inspections will result in a loss of revenue and place a heavy burden on STR owners.

items.title: Mark Reilly, STR owner, Elora appeared in support of the by-law and
notes: feels the Township should improve communication around the benefits of tourism and STRs and monies generated should be put back into community programming.
He supports moderate regulation and feels regulations designed to control the bad behavior of some STR owners shouldn’t apply to all STRs.

items.title: User Group Storage Agreement
notes: Report from L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks

L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks provided an overview of the report, indicating the proposed Indoor/Outdoor User Group Storage Agreement aims to formalize the use of municipal spaces for the storage of items not owned by the Township. He noted it will provide clear guidelines, enhance safety and establish accountability for both the Township and community user groups.

items.title: Fergus Downtown Illumination CIP Grant Stream
notes: Report from C.Turton, Planning and Development Coordinator Kristen Bettiol, Manager of Community Development provided an overview of the report, indicating staff is requesting approval from Council to adopt a new stream of the Centre Wellington Community Improvement Plan (CIP). The proposed stream, called the Fergus Downtown Illumination Grant, would be a new addition to the Centre Wellington CIP program.

items.title: Healthcare Professional Accommodation Update
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, indicating as construction of the new Operations Centre approaches, staff recommend the healthcare professional accommodation is moved from the Gartshore Farmhouse to the Craighead Cottage located at 495 Union Street, West, Fergus. He noted this will minimize the impact on healthcare professionals while construction occurs at the Operations Centre.
